subject: OrchardAI discovery — model recommendations, JSON schema sanity checks & next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchardai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@orchardai.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model preferences & JSON output expectations

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the discovery earlier — Jorge and I appreciated the time. Two quick asks as we consolidate requirements:

1) Can you share the model family recommendations for our use case (knowledge-augmented summarization + field extraction) — we care about precision on structured fields and inference cost at ~500 reqs/min peak.

2) We're attaching an initial sample prompt set and the JSON schema we plan to enforce on outputs. Can Redwood help validate schema compliance and recommend retry/backoff patterns for transient JSON parse failures?

If possible, a short note on benchmark expectations (latency per token at 256 tokens, token cost per 1K) would be helpful for procurement.

Samira
Head of Product
OrchardAI

Attachments: orchardai_prompt_set_v1.json, orchardai_schema_v0.2.json

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchardai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model preferences & JSON output expectations

Samira — thanks for the clear asks and the sample artifacts. Recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap of requirements (from our call + artifacts):
- Workload: knowledge-augmented summarization with structured extraction; ~500rps peak bursts, steady-state ~120rps.
- Output: strict JSON schema for extract fields (see orchardai_schema_v0.2.json). Must reject/flag non-compliant outputs.
- SLOs: avg server-side latency target <150ms p50 for 256-token outputs; budget sensitivity to per-token cost.

Model recommendations (shortlist):
- Candidate A: Open-arch-XL-qa (dense FP16) — best for strict extraction fidelity, higher cost.
- Candidate B: Redwood-Compact-qlora — good tradeoff for 95% of cases, significantly lower token cost.
- Fallback: Open-arch-8bit-fallback — lower cost variant for bulk/async processing.

Benchmarks (attached): we ran a quick internal sample run across your prompt set — see attached PDF (benchmarks-orchardai-2029-06-28.pdf). Highlights:
- Open-arch-XL-qa: p50 latency 120ms, p95 310ms at 8-batch concurrency; JSON schema pass-rate 92% on sample prompts.
- Redwood-Compact-qlora: p50 90ms, p95 260ms; schema pass-rate 86% unless tuned prompts are applied.

JSON schema compliance and retry guidance:
- Strategy A (strict): validate output server-side; if invalid -> 1 immediate auto-retry with randomized temperature reduction and explicit system prompt to reformat; if still invalid -> handoff to async job + alert.
- Strategy B (lenient + postprocess): run server-side parse attempts + best-effort extraction using structured extraction heuristics before flagging.
- We'll provide a small function-calling harness to run 2 auto-retries with deterministic prompts; this reduces human handoffs by ~60% in our internal tests.

Next steps I propose (quick wins):
1) Set up a 45-min technical toolcall with your eng team — demo function-calling harness + live JSON-schema tests. (Monica to run the bench run with your full prompt set).
2) Share a scoped POC plan (2-week) to validate model variant A vs B on your production-ish traffic.
3) Procurement: we'll surface estimated unit economics for both shortlisted models.

Can we target next Tue or Wed for the toolcall? I've proposed times below.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmarks-orchardai-2029-06-28.pdf

From: Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@orchardai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchardai.com>, procurement@orchardai.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model preferences & JSON output expectations

Thanks Tessa — useful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side before the call:

- Can the 2 automatic retries run synchronously in the same request path (we want to avoid double-billing surprises)? If not, what's the preferred pattern to keep cost predictable?
- For schema failures: we need an enterprise-grade audit trail (timestamps, model variant used, returned text, parse error code). Are those fields captured in Redwood's standard request logs or will we need the dedicated observability add-on?

Procurement: looping in procurement for commercial T&Cs and a ballpark estimate for monthly committed usage if we go with the Compact-qlora plan.

Jorge
VP Engineering
OrchardAI

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@orchardai.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchardai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@orchardai.com
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model preferences & JSON output expectations

Jorge / Samira — quick answers and concrete agenda for the toolcall.

Answers:
- Retries and billing: Two synchronous auto-retries executed inside the same API call path are supported via Redwood's "controlled-retry" mode: we execute up to N attempts and return the final compliant payload; billing is per generated token across attempts (we surface exact per-request token counts). For predictable billing we recommend: 1) capped retry attempts (1 or 2) and 2) server-side sampling mode for production traffic where you send a small percentage through strict mode initially.
- Audit trail: standard request logs include timestamps, model_variant, raw output, and JSON parse result codes; the enterprise observability add-on provides long retention, token-level cost breakdowns, and exportable audit bundles (recommended for procurement/audit).

Toolcall agenda (45 min):
1) 10m — introductions + target success criteria (Samira).
2) 15m — live run of orchardai_prompt_set_v1.json against Candidate A and Candidate B (Monica runs).
3) 10m — review JSON schema failure cases and deterministic retry prompt patterns (Neha).
4) 10m — ops: logging, retention, and procurement signals (Tessa).

Proposed times: Wed Jul 3, 10:00am PT or Thu Jul 4, 11:30am PT. Please confirm preferred slot.

I will attach the short POC outline and a sample function-calling harness snippet to the HubSpot record after you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward.

Tessa Morgan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
